public_rationale: For Google, a court exhibit showed Gemini at about 90 million monthly users in October 2024. That is far below ChatGPT and Meta AI, which fits the speaker's point that uptake was weak for Google's reach. But 90 million is a real audience, and the count reached 350 million by March 2025, so 'categorically, unquestionably failed' is hard to sustain on an absolute reading. For Microsoft, I found no first-party consumer Copilot figure for the period to test either way. Both companies spent heavily on capital, but none of it is broken out for consumer Copilot or Gemini, so 'burning billions to do so' cannot be tied to these efforts. The result turns on an unstated threshold for failure, and key data are missing. So it stays unresolved.
limitations: Gemini figures come from a news report of a court slide.
It is unclear whether Google's counts include Gemini inside Workspace or Gmail.
No consumer-only Copilot data were found.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft and Google have failed to drive consumer adoption of Copilot and Gemini while burning billions.

statement.excerpt: While Microsoft and Google may make money outside of consumer software, both companies have desperately tried to cram Copilot and Gemini down consumers' throats, and they have categorically, unquestionably failed, all while burning billions of dollars to do so.

from_speaker: desperately tried to cram Copilot and Gemini down consumers' throats
all while burning billions of dollars to do so
framed by 'neither Gemini nor Copilot has any meaningful consumer penetration'
our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post, consumer uptake of Copilot and Gemini was not meaningful given each company's reach and push, and both companies spent billions on these efforts.
'Failed' is judged by consumer penetration, as the speaker's own setup sentence says, relative to Microsoft's and Google's scale.
'Burning billions' is read as spending attributable to the AI push. The surrounding text cites cumulative capital spending since 2023, so no narrow spending window is imposed.
Adoption target period: October 2024 to February 2025, the latest data before the post. Spending may be cumulative from 2023.
criteria.support_condition: Consumer usage data for the period showing Copilot and Gemini with small audiences relative to the companies' reach and rival chatbots, plus evidence of billions in spending on these efforts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Consumer usage data for the period showing large, meaningful audiences for Copilot or Gemini, or evidence that the spending was not in the billions.

evidence.excerpt: in October 2024, Gemini’s user numbers were 9 million daily and 90 million monthly.
evidence.explanation: About 90 million monthly Gemini users in October 2024 is a sizeable absolute consumer audience. That cuts against 'categorically failed' on an absolute reading.

evidence.excerpt: Meta AI was nearing 500 million monthly users as of September 2024, while OpenAI recently said that its weekly active users top 400 million.
evidence.explanation: Rivals had several times Gemini's audience, which supports the relative reading that Google's consumer push lagged badly.

evidence.excerpt: as of March 2025, Gemini had 350 million monthly users worldwide, and 35 million daily users.
evidence.explanation: Gemini's audience roughly quadrupled to 350 million monthly users within weeks of the post. This is just outside the target period, so it is context only.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: First-party consumer user counts for Copilot and Gemini apps in late 2024 and early 2025, plus any breakout of spending on the consumer products.
